analysis: Both changed files are CI test scripts (.github/scripts/test-threat-bedrock.py and test-threat-budget.py) for the threat-review tooling. They assert new behaviours: Bedrock diagnostics carry request_id/stop_reason/sdk_code without provider message bodies, with a malformed SDK error code collapsing to "RequestFailure"; fallback failures retain the backup call identity; and manual_review_reasons is separate from errors. Tests also assert clean() fails closed when manual_review_reasons is missing (legacy report) or non-empty, that final Sol integration uncertainty never clears, that cross-file uncertainty from local depth is not cleared, that malformed cache entries stop without spend or leaking content, that the Bedrock call cap prevents clearance, and that diagnostics write failures don't destroy the report and are path-free. No product code in the provider, coordinator or cache (T-041 and other threat-model assets) is changed. The security-relevant production logic is in threat_review/* (merge_policy, bedrock, budget_scan, budget_runner), which these units do not include; later passes should check that those modules match the tested fail-closed behaviour. No concrete security regression found in the test changes, and no threat-model gap identified.
